fact: CPJ states that journalists Comlan Hugues Sossoukpè and Ali Moumouni, held without trial for 10 months by 24 May 2026, remained imprisoned on 1 September 2026 on charges including harassment through electronic communications, which CPJ says were brought in retaliation for critical reporting.
CPJ states that journalist Angela Kpeidja was sentenced to 12 months in prison for asking questions on Facebook about the December 2025 coup attempt as it unfolded.

MFWA reports journalist Angela Kpeidja was detained on 16 December 2025 over two Facebook posts questioning the security authorities on the day of the attempted coup, and the special prosecutor sought two years, one firm, on 11 May 2026 under Digital Code Article 550.

The Media Foundation for West Africa reports that editor Olivier Allochémé was arrested on 9 October 2025 and placed in pre-trial detention on 16 October 2025 by the CRIET for 'publishing false news via social media' in a Facebook editorial alleging President Talon had surveilled the former Speaker, with a hearing on 30 October 2025 adjourned to 15 January 2026.

Benin's media professionals' union UPMB and Amnesty International Bénin, meeting on 3 November 2026, called for a review of articles 550 and following of the Code du numérique over their implications for journalists, bloggers and citizens.

RSF states that journalist Pascal Mitowade of La Tribune de la Capitale was sentenced on 24 March 2026 to five years in prison and a 10 million CFA franc fine for 'apology of crimes against state security' over Facebook posts about the 7 December 2025 coup attempt.

RSF states that journalist Angela Kpeidja is being prosecuted for 'harassment via electronic communication' over Facebook posts on the December 2025 coup attempt, and on 11 May 2026 prosecutors sought two years, one to be served.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 12 March 2025 the HAAC indefinitely suspended Benin Web TV and revoked its director's press card after its reports on inconsistencies in the HAAC's 2025 budget, lifting the suspension on 20 May 2025.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 2 June 2025 digital activist Steve Amoussou was sentenced to two years and a two million CFA franc fine for 'politically motivated insult' and 'spreading false information' linked to a Facebook page critical of the government.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 6 June 2025 Les Democrates communications member Julien Kande Kansou was arrested over statements on an 'electoral revolution' and economic monopolies, and on 12 June placed in pretrial detention accused of publishing false news and electronic harassment.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 10 July 2025 journalist Comlan Hugues Sossoukpe, known for criticism of President Talon, was arrested in Abidjan, extradited to Benin on 11 July and charged on 12 July with incitement to rebellion and hatred, cyberstalking and praising terrorism.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 15 July 2025 La Boussole editor Cosme Hounsa was arrested and charged with harassment by electronic means after a minister's complaint over a report on a dispute between ministers.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 22 February 2025 the opposition party Les Democrates condemned the police ban on its 9 February rally and announced plans for legal action against those responsible.
Amnesty, RSF and Internet Sans Frontieres state that the HAAC suspended the newspaper Le Patriote and its website on 21 January 2025 after an editorial on the government's security strategy.

Amnesty, RSF and Internet Sans Frontieres state that the HAAC suspended the news website Benin Web TV on 12 March 2025 over articles on the HAAC's budget request and its president's car request, and withdrew its director's press card.

Le Patriote published an editorial pointing out 'the government's ineffective strategy' during an attack on a military position near the Burkina Faso-Niger border, per Amnesty, RSF and Internet Sans Frontieres.

Fraternite reports that at a Digital Rights Academy workshop on 1 July 2026, jurists, researchers and parliamentarians, including Dr Julien Hounkpe, criticised Article 550 of the Digital Code on false information and called for proportionate sanctions and a targeted reform.

CIVICUS Monitor states that since the December 2025 failed coup, opposition politicians, journalists, activists and social media users have been arrested and prosecuted on charges including incitement to rebellion and electronic harassment, particularly those critical of the government's handling of the crisis.

At a 6 November 2024 parliamentary workshop, Les Democrates MP Raouf Sariki urged a review of the heavy penalties in Benin's digital code, and the civil-society group Observatoire des SIC (Mahoussi) urged amending Article 550 to remove its provisions on abusive content.
Global Voices cites Benin's Ignace Sossou as prosecuted for his posts in 2019.
